payload.claim: `_pull`'s pluralization suffix (the trailing `s` on `"N new failures"`) is never actually checked: the one case that exercises the red-suite message (`verify` returning 2) asserts only `lines[0].startswith(f"{ESCALATE}red suite, 2 new failure")`, a prefix that stops one character before the pluralizing `s`, and no case uses `n == 1` to exercise the singular branch at all. Swapping the suffix logic so plural becomes singular and vice versa keeps every witness in `tests/test_finish.py` passing.
